title: Cross-multiplied numerator equation on two section-ring charts
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $L$ an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], $S$ its section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], $d>0$, $s\in S_d$, $U\subseteq X$ open, and $s|_U$ a free generator [def-sc-local-free-generator]. Let $\rho:S_{(s)}\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ satisfy $\rho(a/s^m)(s^m)|_U=a|_U$ for every $m\geq0$ and $a\in S_{md}$. Let $q:U\to\operatorname{Spec}S_{(s)}$ induce $\rho$ under the canonical identifications [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], and put $g=\iota_s\circ q$ [def-pc-proj]. For every $e>0$, $t\in S_e$, $n\geq0$ and $\xi\in S_{ne}$, put $W=\operatorname{image}_X(g^{-1}D_+(t))$, $k=n(d-1)$, and $a=g^\sharp(\xi/t^n)\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_X)$. Then $a\,\mu((t^n)|_W\otimes(t^k)|_W)=(\xi t^k)|_W$ in $\Gamma(W,L^{\otimes(ne+ke)})$, where $\mu$ is the section-ring tensor multiplication $L^{\otimes ne}\otimes L^{\otimes ke}\cong L^{\otimes(ne+ke)}$ [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. The extra tensor factor is not cancelled in this statement.

proof.text: Put i=ne, j=n(d-1)e and η=ξ*t^(n(d-1)). This numerator has degree i+j=ned. On the intersection of the s- and t-charts set r=t^d/s^e. The homogeneous fraction identity (ξ/t^n)*r^n=η/s^(ne) follows by multiplying numerators and denominators and n+n(d-1)=nd.

source.place: Tags 01N8 (local quotient construction and comparison) and 01NK (different positive degrees)

proof.text: Pull the fraction identity back along q. Restriction from the s-chart is localization at r; hq identifies the map on global sections with ρ. On a local basis z of L write s=b*z^d and t=c*z^e; hs makes b a unit. The two applications of hρ to η and t^d give a*(c^d/b^e)^n=η_coeff/b^(ne). Multiply by b^(ne), a unit, to obtain a*c^(nd)=η_coeff. No cancellation of c is needed.

source.place: Tags 01N8 (local quotient construction and comparison) and 01NK (different positive degrees)

proof.text: Tensor multiplication and tensorPowAddIso identify c^(nd)*z^(ned) with the product of the restricted sections t^n and t^k. Naturality of these maps turns the local coefficient equality into the displayed equality in L.tensorPow(i+j); sheaf separation glues the local identities. The exponent-zero, d=1 and empty-open cases obey the same formulas.
